title: The potential: can do
summary: The potential る / られる attaches to the え-stem and makes an ichidan verb. The thing that is possible takes が, as 好き did in lesson 9.

blocks.text: The **potential** says that you **can** do something. It is one of the **helper words** from lesson 7.5: it attaches to the **え-stem** and says that the action is **possible**.

For **godan** verbs the helper is just the single kana **る**, added to the え-stem. For **ichidan** verbs it is **られる**. Either way the result is an **ichidan verb**, so it changes like one. The potential of する is the separate verb **できる**; written 出来る, it means "comes out", so "Japanese comes out (is possible) for me".
Note that 来 changes its reading: 来る is read **くる**, but 来られる is read **こられる**.

blocks.title: The potential changes like an ichidan verb

blocks.text: The potential says that something **is possible**, so the thing that is possible is the main carriage and takes **が**. 本が読める is literally "the book is readable".
本が読める。 (I) can read the book (the book is readable).
日本語ができる。 (I) can do Japanese (Japanese comes out, it is possible).

With a hidden carriage, the zero is again the speaker, just like 食べたい in lesson 9: 読める on its own means "(I) can read". You can also put 私 in front as a topic. A sentence like 私が本を読める is possible, but it puts the person first the way English does, and it sounds less Japanese.

blocks.title: Remember
items: Godan: **え-stem + る** (買う → 買える). Ichidan: **drop る + られる**.
来る → **来られる** (こられる); する → **できる**.
The result is an **ichidan verb**: 歩ける, 歩けない, 歩けた, 歩けなかった.
The thing that is possible takes **が**: **本が読める**.
